subject: Post-call: Hyperscaler comparison & next evaluation steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@avery.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hyperscaler comparison & next evaluation steps

Sam — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the competitive points you asked us to follow up on. I consolidated the concrete next steps below so we have a shared checklist.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Avery is evaluating Redwood vs their current hyperscaler endpoints (AWS/GCP-based inference) for customer-facing summarization and Q&A.
- Primary concerns: short-tail latency (P95), hallucination rate on domain facts, throughput cost at scale, and regional data residency.
- Avery will run an apples-to-apples evaluation and asked for: recommended prompt set, suggested model/config baselines, and a test harness that measures latency/cost/hallucination.

Proposed next tests we committed to:
1) Latency P95 test: 1k realtime-style requests (avg 100-300 tokens), measure P50/P95/P99 and cold vs warm latencies. (owner: Stephanie)
2) Hallucination/regression checks: 200 domain-specific fact prompts, plus 50 adversarial prompts. Compare hallucination rate vs their hyperscaler baseline. (owner: Rishi)
3) Quality parity run: run our curated eval prompts with identical sampling settings (temperature/top_p) and return token-by-token logs for analysis. (owner: Laura)
4) Cost-throughput simulation: synthetic burst workload to model token cost at target throughput (50 reqs/sec sustained). We'll provide cost breakdown per 1M tokens. (owner: Marcus)

Attachments: evaluation plan spreadsheet and the sample prompts file. I also dropped a Drive link to the working folder.

Ask for Avery: Sam, please confirm which hyperscaler endpoint(s) and model flavors you want us to mirror for the baseline (Bedrock/Vertex/Azure). Also confirm whether the tests should run from us-east-1 only or include eu/eur regions.

Next meeting: propose Thurs 3/4 10am PT to review initial numbers.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Marcus — thanks for the thorough recap. This looks good and matches internal notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline: please mirror Bedrock (gpt-neo-3-small equivalent) and Vertex (text-bison) settings. We'll provide API endpoints and a dump of 50 recent user queries to seed the test.
- Regions: start with us-east-1; if results look promising we'll ask for an eu-west-1 run.
- Reporting: can you include a simple CSV export with per-prompt verdict (pass/fail/hallucinated) plus the Redwood generated text? Our CS analyst will ingest it.

Also — two asks: can you run Hallucination tests with both temperature 0 and 0.2, and include the model logits if feasible? That will help our forensic team.

Confirming Thurs 3/4 10am PT. Appreciate the attachments — I'll share the internal query dump to the Drive folder you linked.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Hyperscaler comparison & next evaluation steps

Looping in the technical plan and quick notes on measurement methodology.

Laura — for the regression checks I propose the following specifics so results are reproducible:
- Baselines: run Redwood default-gen-small (cpu-quant) and our dedicated-accelerated variant (gpu-fast) to show delta.
- Sampling: temperature=0 and temperature=0.2; top_p=0.95; max_tokens=256.
- Prompts: use the provided avery_sample_prompts.jsonl (200 prompts). We'll add 50 adversarial strings that are close paraphrases of true facts.
- Metrics: hallucination_rate (binary), factual_precision (manual eval sampling), token_efficiency (tokens per useful token), latency P95.

Data capture plan:
- We'll log full response + token-level timestamps to compute warm vs cold fill times.
- If Sam can provide the hyperscaler endpoints, we'll run the harness against them in parallel from the same test runner to reduce noise.

Work division: Rishi will run the hallucination/regression harness and produce an initial CSV within 48 hours. Laura will take the quality parity and produce side-by-side diff snippets for the most discrepant 20 prompts. Stephanie will spin up the latency-focused Dedicated test config (autoscale disabled, fixed pool) and share provisioning notes. Marcus will handle cost extrapolations and the deck for Thursday.

I'll start the harness this afternoon against Redwood endpoints and keep Sam updated in the Drive folder.

- Rishi
Senior Applied Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
